weather.subtitle: Current conditions, a 7-day outlook, and plain-language advice on what to wear, how to plan the day and what to carry.
weather.adviceTitle: What this means for your visit
weather.noAlert: No particular risk today — conditions are comfortable for a visit.
weather.unavailable: Live weather is unavailable right now. Please check back shortly.
weather.marketNote: The walking street runs 17:00–22:00, so the evening numbers matter most.

advice.alertThunder: Thunderstorms are likely: do not wait one out on the riverbank or under a tree, and expect boat trips and river activities to be suspended.
advice.alertHeavyRain: Heavy rain: the river steps and low-lying lanes may flood — keep away from the water's edge and the rock shelves.
advice.alertWind: Strong wind: stay clear of signs, trees and riverside rocks, and hold on to umbrellas and hats.
advice.alertHeat: Extreme heat: avoid long spells outdoors between 11:00 and 15:00, and drink water often.
advice.alertFog: Poor visibility: the morning mist is thick, so use lights and ride slowly. Distant views will be obscured.
advice.alertWindy: Breezy: the riverside feels cooler than the town, and a long umbrella is awkward to manage.
advice.alertHeatWarn: Hot: take care around midday and move the walk to the early morning or the evening.
advice.alertUV: Strong UV: reapply sunscreen if you stay outdoors for long.
advice.alertSlippery: Slippery surfaces: boardwalks, steps and rocks turn slick in the rain.
advice.outfitHot: Hot weather — light, breathable clothing works best.
advice.outfitWarm: Warm — short sleeves are fine, with a thin layer for air-conditioned shops.
advice.outfitMild: Comfortable — a light long-sleeve shirt, or short sleeves with a thin jacket.
advice.outfitCool: Cooler at both ends of the day — bring a light jacket.
advice.outfitCold: Cold — dress warm and take a thicker jacket.
advice.outfitDiurnal: A day-to-night swing of about {range}°C — layer up so you can adjust.
advice.outfitRain: Rain expected — a water-resistant jacket and grippy shoes make the walk easier.
advice.outfitHumid: Humid and muggy — breathable, quick-dry clothing is more comfortable.
advice.outfitWind: Breezy — avoid loose long skirts and hats that lift off in the wind.
advice.outfitCover: For the temples, keep shoulders and knees covered; a shawl is handy to carry.
advice.planThunder: Pause outdoor activity. Do not shelter on the riverbank or under a tree during a storm.
advice.planHeavyRain: Long spells outdoors are not advised; avoid the bank, the steps and the rock shelves.
advice.planRain: Rain is likely — favour the stretch where the shophouses give cover, as open-air stalls may close early.
advice.planHeat: Midday is hot: shift the walk to early morning or after 17:00.
advice.planWind: The riverside catches more wind — mind parasols, hats and light items.
advice.planSlippery: After rain the boardwalks and steps are slippery — wear grippy shoes and slow down.
advice.planEvening: Rain is possible during market hours — starting before 17:00 gives you a drier window.
advice.planIndoor: If it rains, move into the shophouses and cafés along the street and keep exploring under cover.
advice.planSunny: Clear and pleasant — ideal for walking the river road and waiting for the sunset.
advice.planOvercast: Overcast and free of harsh sun — comfortable for a long walk and good for photographing the facades.
advice.planPartly: Sun and cloud together, so the light stays soft — good for photographing the old houses.
advice.planMist: Humidity is high before dawn, so mist often lies on the river — a good photography window, but visibility is low.
advice.planSunset: Cloud cover looks suitable, so the sunset should be visible — be on the bank by about 18:00.
advice.planNoSunset: Thick cloud today makes a clear sunset unlikely.
advice.planInsect: Warm and damp — mosquitoes are active by the river at dusk, so trousers are more comfortable.
advice.itemFoldingUmbrella: A folding umbrella — showers are possible.
advice.itemRaincoat: A raincoat — more practical than a long umbrella in this wind.
advice.envRiversideBank: The river may rise — do not linger on the water steps or the rock shelves.
advice.envRiversideWind: The open water makes the wind stronger than in town, and the evening feels cooler.
advice.envUrbanShelter: Shophouses along the street offer shelter, so you can switch to an indoor stretch if it rains.
advice.envUrbanHeat: The dense buildings make midday feel hotter than the open bank — keep to the shaded side.
advice.envMountainTemp: The hills are noticeably cooler than the town — dress for a lower temperature.
advice.envMountainView: Visibility is good — a fine day to head for a lookout point.
advice.envMountainStorm: Heavy rain risk in the hills: beware flash floods and landslides, and postpone the climb.
advice.envForestTrail: Forest trails turn muddy and slippery after rain — watch your footing.
advice.envForestInsect: Insects are active in the woods — long trousers and repellent help.
advice.envCoastalWind: The sea is running rough — follow local maritime and lifeguard notices and do not enter the water on your own.
advice.envCoastalSwim: With thunderstorms or strong wind, swimming and the rock areas are off limits.
advice.envCoastalUV: UV is stronger at the coast and reflects off the water — step up your sun protection.
advice.envCaveTemp: Caves stay cool and damp all year — add a jacket before going in.
advice.envCaveSlick: In rain the cave floor and steps are slippery — hold the rail and move slowly.
advice.envDesertDust: Windy and dry, with dust likely in the air — a mask and eye protection help.
advice.envDesertDiurnal: Desert day-to-night swings are extreme: sun protection by day, warm layers for the night.
